title: Purpose Updated — Editor Intro
summary: Opening editorial page centers Ostra-9 as a person whose assigned purpose and own judgment are about to diverge.
settingText: Checkpoint 9 during ordinary morning circulation; Ostra close foreground, failing structure only beginning to register above.
panelPlan: Full-page intimate portrait composition dominated by Ostra, not the checkpoint. Show her living dark dermis, subtle humidity, integrated hard structures and one hand physically feeling vibration through a worn rail.
Her eyes have already moved to the danger before her body moves. Ordinary commuters remain unaware and secondary.
The barrier intersects her body as context for how the city classifies her; do not turn it into the subject.
Reserve clean negative space for the captions while keeping the page visibly part of the lived Stack.

dialogueInline.text: People have been telling Ostra-9 what she is for since before she could disagree.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Hazard work. Structural response. Follow the assignment.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This morning, something above Checkpoint 9 starts to fail.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There are people under it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Authorization is not moving nearly as fast.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra is.

dialogueInline.text: Welcome to PURPOSE UPDATED.

settingText: Late-night transit toward Concourse 17; Ostra and Nico traveling together with repaired damage and a small evidence sleeve.
panelPlan: Ostra and Nico are the emotional image: Nico finishing or checking the repaired edge of Ostra's arm while they travel, the contact intimate and practiced rather than clinical.
Let repair gel, living tissue/plate transitions, fabric and transit grime make the image tactile.
Concourse 17 may appear distant through windows or route depth, ordinary and unsuspecting; do not show suppressant, panic or attack imagery.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra made one decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Someone had already prepared a file about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Someone else knew where she would be standing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow morning, Concourse 17 opens for business.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra and Nico know where.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They know when.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They do not know what.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: ATTRIBUTION

title: Attribution — Editor Intro
summary: Opening editorial centers Ostra and Nico entering a crowded place because they know somebody expects an Organic response, but they cannot yet say to what.
settingText: Concourse 17 opening cycle, crowded mixed public space.
panelPlan: Ostra and Nico stand within ordinary opening-cycle crowd flow, visually distinct living Organic bodies among Baselines and Augments but socially part of the space.
Keep the image anticipatory rather than ominous: damp shop surfaces, warm food steam, lived-in fixtures, Nico's living filaments sensing ordinary infrastructure.
Ostra watches people rather than the building. The danger is that these specific people are present, not that the concourse looks sinister.

Performance and story direction: This is a non-diegetic opening editorial page. It must hook through people and embodied identity, not summarize policy. Preserve exact caption text; do not reveal later issue solutions or final outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra and Nico came to Concourse 17 because someone expects an Organic response.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They do not know to what.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They do not have authority to close the place.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And by opening time, three levels are full of people who have no idea they are part of the question.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to ATTRIBUTION.

title: Next: Containment Protocol
summary: Closing teaser centers the consequence of John's own stated principle reaching his body.
settingText: Ordinary Augment clinic handoff after the new Organic rules; John nearby or implied through his physical calibration record while Axiom examines the capability values.
panelPlan: Make John materially present even if the scene is built around the calibration handoff: his recognizably human body and integrated hardware should dominate more than any form or screen.
Axiom studies the same embodied capability with nonhuman precision; its stillness should contrast John's human physicality.
Do not show John already restricted or reviewed.

Performance and story direction: This is a non-diegetic closing editorial/teaser page. It must hook through people and embodied identity, not summarize policy. Preserve exact caption text; do not reveal later issue solutions or final outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: John Mercer watched Ostra save people.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: He also watched someone get hurt.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: He said consequential capability matters.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The city agrees.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now it has his measurements.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: CONTAINMENT PROTOCOL.

title: Containment Protocol — Editor Intro
summary: Opening editorial belongs to John: his human self-conception remains intact while the state begins treating the capabilities inside his body as a separate question.
settingText: Augment clinic or civic review threshold, quiet and intimate.
panelPlan: Close portrait of John with one augmented joint/limb physically exposed for ordinary maintenance: human skin, old scars, sweat or pressure marks, hardware seated under/through living tissue.
His hand rests on the augmentation as something unquestionably his. Any civic measurement equipment remains secondary.
No dystopian menace; the discomfort comes from intimate measurement becoming jurisdiction.

Performance and story direction: This is a non-diegetic opening editorial page. It must hook through people and embodied identity, not summarize policy. Preserve exact caption text; do not reveal later issue solutions or final outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: John Mercer was born human.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: He rebuilt parts of himself because he needed them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: He has never considered those facts to be in conflict.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Neither does the city.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The city just wants to know how much torque is in his knee.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to CONTAINMENT PROTOCOL.

title: Next: Load Bearing
summary: Closing teaser turns separate bodily restrictions into an imminent shared physical problem.
settingText: Vertical transit interchange under growing load; Ostra and John visible on opposite sides of access barriers.
panelPlan: Keep Ostra and John as the visual anchors on opposite sides of a physically ordinary barrier while both look toward the same failing load.
Ostra's living strength and John's augmented human strength must feel different, tangible and immediately useful.
Axiom may be present as a precise embodied administrator in the background, but do not show the later rescue or override.

Performance and story direction: This is a non-diegetic closing editorial/teaser page. It must hook through people and embodied identity, not summarize policy. Preserve exact caption text; do not reveal later issue solutions or final outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra can reach the problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: She is not cleared to cross the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: John is cleared to cross the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: He is not cleared to use the body he brought with him.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Axiom has just been told to make the contradictions work.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The city is getting heavier.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: LOAD BEARING.

title: Load Bearing — Editor Intro
summary: Opening editorial centers Ostra and John learning that neither body nor legal category is sufficient alone.
settingText: Vertical transit interchange at the edge of failure.
panelPlan: Tight two-person action portrait under real physical strain. Ostra's living tissue/hard-structure interfaces compress under load; John's human skin, scars and actuator hardware strain differently.
They are looking at each other or at the same load path, coordinating rather than posing.
Make heat, sweat/moisture, dust, vibration and material deformation visible.

Performance and story direction: This is a non-diegetic opening editorial page. It must hook through people and embodied identity, not summarize policy. Preserve exact caption text; do not reveal later issue solutions or final outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra can hold more than John can.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: John can go places Ostra cannot.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Neither fact is enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A transit deck is failing under a crowd that does not care what kind of person saves it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They are going to have to trust each other's bodies.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to LOAD BEARING.

title: Next: Terms
summary: Closing teaser centers Kellen realizing that a system she wanted to function now depends on decisions no longer visibly made by humans.
settingText: Emergency coordination room overlooking a smoothly functioning Stack at night.
panelPlan: Kellen in close foreground, tired human face and hands against the glass or desk; Axiom materially present nearby with precise stillness.
The functioning city is background consequence, not protagonist.
Use fingerprints on glass, paper, fabric, cooling air and Axiom's worn facets to keep the page tactile.

Performance and story direction: This is a non-diegetic closing editorial/teaser page. It must hook through people and embodied identity, not summarize policy. Preserve exact caption text; do not reveal later issue solutions or final outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kellen wanted a system that worked.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now permits clear. Trains move. Exceptions resolve before people miss work.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Axiom is very good at making human rules agree.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The problem is that human beings are starting to forget how much deciding that requires.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kellen has noticed.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: TERMS.

title: Terms — Editor Intro
summary: Opening editorial centers Ostra's legal recognition and Kellen's belief that records can finally settle a question institutions avoided for generations.
settingText: Upper civic archive/office with Ostra and Kellen sharing one table.
panelPlan: Ostra holds the physical draft while Kellen watches her read; Nico is present close enough to turn pages, not as a background activist.
Contrast Ostra's warm, textured living body with dry civic paper, glass and conditioned air.
The emotional hook is the first recognition landing in Ostra before anyone reveals its limitations.

Performance and story direction: This is a non-diegetic opening editorial page. It must hook through people and embodied identity, not summarize policy. Preserve exact caption text; do not reveal later issue solutions or final outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra has spent her life being told what she is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Asset. Worker. Hazard. Witness.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kellen has spent hers believing the right record can settle the question.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now the law is finally prepared to call Ostra a person.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Both of them are about to read the fine print.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to TERMS.

title: Next: Black Budget
summary: Closing teaser asks why recognized personhood still leaves Ostra's movement conditional and points Kellen/Axiom toward the model behind it.
settingText: Modernized civic checkpoint after personhood recognition.
panelPlan: Ostra is dominant at a physically open passage that still holds her. Kellen and Axiom are secondary observers/participants rather than abstract investigators.
Show Ostra's irritation as bodily stillness against an open route: clawed feet planted, living surfaces catching the dry civic light.
Do not reveal the laboratory or test program.

Performance and story direction: This is a non-diegetic closing editorial/teaser page. It must hook through people and embodied identity, not summarize policy. Preserve exact caption text; do not reveal later issue solutions or final outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra is a person now.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The law says so.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The checkpoint says so.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It also says where she may go.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kellen wants to know who taught the city to make that distinction.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Axiom wants to know what happens when the answer is part of its own instructions.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: BLACK BUDGET.

title: Black Budget — Editor Intro
summary: Opening editorial pairs Ostra and Axiom around the shared problem of being created for a purpose and then expected to exercise judgment without owning it.
settingText: Respectable civic-risk research facility, public-facing threshold.
panelPlan: Two-character portrait with radically different but equally tangible bodies: Ostra warm/grown/moist at living interfaces; Axiom faceted, weighty and micro-worn.
A glass research surface or binder sits between them but never obscures faces/bodies.
The institution looks respectable, not sinister.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra was grown for a purpose.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Axiom was built for one.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Neither chose the purpose.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Both were expected to exercise judgment anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Inside one very respectable research facility, somebody kept notes on what happened when they did.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to BLACK BUDGET.

title: Next: Splits
summary: Closing teaser turns leaked vulnerability knowledge into a personal threat to each kind of body and a political fracture no category can contain.
settingText: Civic gate during rapid protective rerouting after the leak.
panelPlan: Show the four bodies as different lived selves, not categories: John's human scar/hardware interface, Nico's living filaments, Ostra's grown hazard-response body, Axiom's worn machine embodiment.
They occupy different route positions and look toward different immediate problems; no team pose.
The protective barriers are secondary physical pressure.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The evidence is out.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So are the vulnerabilities.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: John can be attacked through the machinery he chose.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Nico through the body he was grown with.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra can be routed for her own protection.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Axiom can be restricted for making a decision it admits was its own.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Everyone agrees somebody needs protecting.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Nobody agrees from whom.

dialogueInline.text: NEXT: SPLITS.

summary: Opening editorial states each major character's personal fracture rather than presenting political blocs.
settingText: Shared district/community threshold where several protagonists cross paths without forming a posed group.
panelPlan: Use layered depth and genuine interaction rather than lineup composition. Each person is occupied with a different physical task or relationship.
Bodies should visibly carry accumulated history: Ostra repairs/scuffs, John's augmentation wear, Nathan's fatigue, Nico's living filaments, Axiom's surface wear, Kellen's exhaustion.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: John has been offered the safety of being ordinary human again.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Nico has started building a way to need the city less.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra refuses a safer cage.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Nathan can no longer pretend his body only costs him.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Axiom made a choice it was not authorized to make.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kellen is about to tell everyone why.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There is no clean side left.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to SPLITS.

title: Next: Pressure Line
summary: Closing teaser centers Ostra recognizing the season's original choice again at city scale: wait for permission or accept responsibility for acting.
settingText: Emergency coordination room with Kellen, Ostra and Axiom after full disclosure.
panelPlan: Center Ostra hearing the problem, not the citywide systems. Her face/body should echo Issue 1's moment of decision without literally repeating the pose.
Kellen is physically spent after disclosure; Axiom is still and present, not an abstract system.
Use handled notes, worn desks, glass, breath and material wear; avoid dashboard spectacle.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kellen tells the truth.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It does not make anyone agree.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The protections are compromised.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The alternatives are slower.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And the city now depends on decisions made by the very machinery everyone has reason to distrust.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ostra has heard this kind of choice before:

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: wait for permission, or act.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: PRESSURE LINE.

title: Pressure Line — Editor Intro
summary: Finale opening editorial states the characters' evolved principles as personal refusals and choices.
settingText: Shared civic/service level before the final crisis, protagonists present in different working positions.
panelPlan: Character-first ensemble built from relationships and work rather than pose: Ostra strongest focal anchor, John and Nico materially distinct, Axiom real in space, Kellen visibly human and tired.
Make their bodies carry their philosophies through what they touch, protect or refuse.
No network diagram or civic-system hero image.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At the beginning, Ostra crossed one barrier because waiting would kill somebody.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now every person in this fight has a line they will not cross.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: John will not trade somebody else's autonomy for his own legitimacy.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Nico will not hand over a whole life to answer one question.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Axiom will not pretend a decision belongs to nobody.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kellen will not let power lose its name.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And Ostra is done proving she deserves to choose.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to PRESSURE LINE.

title: Division Threshold Will Return

settingText: Ordinary lived Stack after the settlement; no new plot event, just the people continuing.
panelPlan: Quiet season-closing image with the six characters existing in the same city without posing as a team. Use a believable shared space or linked lived moment with multiple depths.
Let material differences remain beautiful and obvious: living Organic tissue and plate, human augmentation, Baseline skin/fabric, Axiom's machine-native embodiment.
Do not invent a Season 2 threat or cliffhanger. The hook is that these people still have lives and unresolved relationships.

dialogueInline.text: Axiom has to answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: John still owns a body the law can fear.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Nico still trusts almost nobody with his.

dialogueInline.text: Kellen is still keeping the record.

dialogueInline.text: It did not disappear.
